title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Drake Maye loses three turnovers in blowout loss Sunday
items.desc: Drake Maye completed 14-of-25 passing attempts for 199 yards and two interceptions while adding 18 yards and a lost fumble on the ground in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
items.impact: Maye's nightmare start to the season continued on Sunday. He lost three turnovers over the course of the afternoon and was only able to lead the Patriots to six points in a blowout loss to the Jaguars. He is unstartable at this point in the season, and fantasy managers should be avoiding most of the fantasy options on New England's offense until they can figure things out.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaguars D/ST stellar in blowout win Sunday
items.desc: The Jaguars' D/ST logged three sacks, two interceptions, and one fumble recovery while allowing just six points in Sunday's blowout win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Jacksonville's defense absolutely shut down the Patriots' offense on Sunday. They allowed just six points over the course of the afternoon and were able to log a number of big plays to help out their own offense. This unit has a tough matchup coming up against the Bengals next week, however, so they may not be worth starting despite their great performance this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cam Little totals five points in win Sunday
items.desc: Cam Little made all five of his extra-point attempts and missed his lone field-goal attempt from 70 yards out in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Little ended up with just five points on Sunday, which is a little disappointing considering how easily scoring came to the Jaguars against New England. He also barely missed one kick from what would have been an NFL record 70-yards out, which further hurt his fantasy total in this matchup. He should bounce back in the near future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chris Rodriguez Jr. finds end zone Sunday
items.desc: Chris Rodriguez Jr. rushed the ball eight times for 37 times and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Rodriguez was clearly the RB2 for the Jaguars on Sunday, but he was still able to contribute quite effectively for them with 37 yards and a touchdown on just eight carries. Still, his current workload won't be enough to offer any sustained fantasy success anytime soon.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brenton Strange catches three passes Sunday
items.desc: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Strange was a solid contributor for the Jaguars on Sunday, hauling in three passes en route to a big win over the Patriots. Still, he isn't a strong fantasy option and shouldn't be considered startable for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jakobi Meyers leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Meyers had a fantastic game against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards over the course of the afternoon and was also able to score a touchdown, which was the cherry on top. This was a good game for the veteran, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to put up numbers like this week-in and week-out moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. quiet in blowout win Sunday
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. caught one pass for eight yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Thomas was a complete non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass over the course of the afternoon, and he was only able to turn that into eight yards on a day that Jacksonville's offense had no trouble scoring and moving the ball. He still has some potential given his talent, but he hasn't been productive for a while and shouldn't be started for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Parker Washington hauls in touchdown Sunday
items.desc: Parker Washington hauled in 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Washington was slightly underwhelming in terms of receptions and yardage on Sunday, but he was able to find the end zone against New England, which left him with a nice fantasy total once again. He has been very good to start the season and should continue to be started in nearly all leagues for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Kelly Kirby
items.title: J.J. McCarthy traded to Giants
items.desc: The Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on Monday for a fifth-round pick.
items.impact: McCarthy's tenure in Minnesota was a rocky one, with injuries and underperformance plaguing the start of his career. However, he may find more opportunity in New York due to the absence of Jaxson Dart and the team's interest in possibly giving McCarthy a shot at the starting job; otherwise, he will serve as Jameis Winston's backup. He can stay on the fantasy waiver wire unless he lands the starting job.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Bhayshul Tuten leads team in rushing Sunday
items.desc: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 15 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 17 yards in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Tuten had a good game on Sunday. He led the team in rushing yards at an efficient clip of 4.9 yards per carry, and he was also able to get into the end zone at one point, which left him with a great fantasy total. He should again be started in a matchup against the Bengals next week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in blowout win Sunday
items.desc: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 passing attempts for 182 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding 25 yards on the ground in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Lawrence played a stellar game on Sunday, finishing with over 200 total yards and three touchdowns in a big win over the Patriots. He has been playing well so far this season and will continue to be a viable starting option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Titans D/ST allows 12 points Sunday
items.desc: The Titans' D/ST logged three sacks and allowed 12 points in Sunday's loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Tennessee's defense had an up-and-down game on Sunday. They did well by holding the Giants to just 12 points on the day, but they weren't able to log any big plays to help out their own offense. This unit should not be started in even the best of matchups moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joey Slye misses one kick Sunday
items.desc: Joey Slye missed his lone field-goal attempt but knocked in his lone extra-point attempt in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Slye didn't play well on Sunday, leaving three points out on the field with a missed field goal against the Giants. He will not be a good fantasy option at the kicker position moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Gunnar Helm quiet in loss Sunday
items.desc: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-4 targets for just 14 yards in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Tennessee's offense as a whole wasn't able to get anything going on Sunday, so it's no surprise that Helm had a bad game. Despite some flashes in the past, fantasy managers shouldn't have much hope for his fantasy output in the future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Elic Ayomanor held to 11 yards Sunday
items.desc: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for just 11 yards in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Ayomanor had a nice showing in Week 2, but he followed that up with a very poor performance in Week 3, being held to just 11 yards in a loss to the Giants. Fantasy managers should feel no desire to roster him at this point in the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Calvin Ridley catchless in loss Sunday
items.desc: Calvin Ridley failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Ridley was a complete non-factor on Sunday, failing to record even a single catch in the team's loss to the Giants. He should not be considered a relevant fantasy option in any league formats moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyjae Spears aggravates ankle injury in loss Sunday
items.desc: Tyjae Spears carried the ball three times for five yards in before leaving the game with an ankle issue in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Spears came into the game on the injury report due to an ankle issue, but he was active and saw three carries for the Titans before re-aggravating the issue. It could cause him to miss some actual time, which would be good news for the fantasy value of Tony Pollard in the meantime.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Wan'Dale Robinson finds end zone Sunday
items.desc: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Robinson played well against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets and receptions against the Giants, and he also scored the team's only touchdown over the course of the afternoon. Despite the good game, fantasy managers should not consider him a viable option moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Carnell Tate leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Carnell Tate hauled in 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: The rookie was arguably the lone bright spot for the Titans on Sunday. He led the team with 58 receiving yards on the afternoon and flashed some real talent in the process. He's a good player but isn't likely to be a consistent fantasy producer on this offense, which is among the NFL's worst.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Bills D/ST quiet in Week 3
items.desc: The Bills D/ST registered two sacks while also forcing one turnover (one interception) in a 24-16 win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3.
items.impact: The defense made up for a surprising five giveaways by their offense, allowing just one touchdown in a winning effort. The unit will look to take advantage of a New England Patriots offense with turnover issues of their own in Week 4.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tony Pollard solid in loss Sunday
items.desc: Tony Pollard rushed the ball 17 times for 74 yards and caught four passes for 22 yards in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Pollard saw the vast majority of carries for the Titans on Sunday with Tyjae Spears (ankle) still dealing with the fallout of his injury. The veteran looked pretty good on Sunday, finishing with nearly 100 total yards over the course of the afternoon. Still, the ineffectiveness of Tennessee's offense will render him an untrustworthy fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cam Ward underwhelming in loss Sunday
items.desc: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passing attempts for 181 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
items.impact: Ward wasn't able to get much going for Tennessee's offense on Sunday. They scored just seven points in this loss to the Giants, and he surrendered one turnover in the process. He has had a rough start to the season and is unlikely to support many good fantasy options on this offense moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Giants D/ST forces two turnovers Sunday
items.desc: The Giants' D/ST logged one interception and one fumble recovery while allowing seven points in Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: New York's defense held the Titans to just seven points on Sunday, which ultimately led to the Giants escaping with a win despite scoring just 12 points themselves. This unit lost Brian Burns (knee) in the process, however, as he is likely to miss the rest of the season with what is suspected to be a torn ACL. His absence will significantly hurt their defensive front and pass rush moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dominic Zvada totals 12 points in win Sunday
items.desc: Dominic Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Zvada was one of the lone bright spots for New York on Sunday, making all four of his kicks and accounting for all of New York's points en route to a narrow win over the Titans. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option at the kicker position moving forward, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. uninvolved in win Sunday
items.desc: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed the ball just one time for three yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: It looks like the veteran has been nearly entirely phased out of this offense. He saw just one opportunity on Sunday and was completely outmatched by Najee Harris, who himself saw nine. Tracy won't be a relevant name in this backfield for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Chargers D/ST disruptive in Week 3 loss
items.desc: The Chargers D/ST forced five turnovers while also recording four sacks in a 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.
items.impact: The defense made up for an underwhelming performance from their offense, allowing less than 200 passing yards in a losing effort. The unit will look for more success in a tough Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Najee Harris efficient in win Sunday
items.desc: Najee Harris rushed the ball nine times for 52 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: The Giants were able to get Harris going on Sunday. He totaled 52 yards on just nine carries, which left him with an efficient clip of 5.8 yards per carry. He's still behind Cam Skattebo on this offense and isn't likely to be fantasy relevant moving forward, but he could eat more and more into the workload in this backfield if he continues to play well.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Chiefs D/ST records four sacks in Week 3
items.desc: The Chiefs D/ST recorded four sacks while also forcing two turnovers (one interception, one fumble recovery) in a 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3.
items.impact: The defense made stops when it needed to, allowing just one touchdown despite giving up 329 offensive yards in the win. The unit will look for more impactful plays against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darnell Mooney ineffective in win Sunday
items.desc: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: New York's offense failed to score even  a single touchdown on Sunday, so it's no surprise that Mooney individually didn't have a good showing either. He caught just two passes for 20 yards, and fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to return to relevance for however long QB Jameis Winston is starting for the Giants.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Malachi Fields catches two passes Sunday
items.desc: Malachi Fields caught two passes for 19 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: The rookie only caught two passes on Sunday, but considering the very low offensive output of New York's offense as a whole, it doesn't come as much of a surprise. He has flashed some talent over the first few weeks of the season, but his poor situation renders him an irrelevant fantasy option moving forward.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Dolphins D/ST forces one turnover in Week 3
items.desc: The Dolphins D/ST forced one turnover (one interception) while failing to record a sack in a 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 3.
items.impact: The unit did what it could to slow down a dynamic Kansas City ground attack, allowing 3.5 yards per carry in a losing effort. The defense will look for a more impactful performance in Week 4 against the Minnesota Vikings.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Isaiah Likely quiet in win Sunday
items.desc: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-5 targets for just 13 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: The veteran wasn't able to get much going on Sunday, finishing with just 13 yards in the team's narrow win over the Titans. He isn't likely to return to fantasy relevance for however long QB Jameis Winston is starting for New York, however, so fantasy managers shouldn't have any hesitations to drop him at this point.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Seahawks D/ST quiet in Week 3
items.desc: The Seahawks D/ST recorded two sacks while failing to force any turnovers in a 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
items.impact: The unit fell victim to a Seattle offense that turned the ball over three times in the loss. The defense will look to get back to its aggressive scheme in a Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Malik Nabers underwhelming in win Sunday
items.desc: Malik Nabers hauled in 5-of-6 targets for just 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Nabers led the team with six targets on Sunday, but he was only able to turn that into five catches for a measly 26 yards over the course of the afternoon. He's a very talented player, but it looks like his fantasy output is going to be sparse for the foreseeable future with QB Jameis Winston currently at the helm for the Giants.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Commanders D/ST forces three turnovers in Week 3 win
items.desc: The Commanders D/ST forced three turnovers (two interceptions, one fumble recovery) and scored a touchdown in a 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: The unit made up for an otherwise forgettable day from a defense that allowed four touchdowns through the air, returning one their two interceptions for a 50-yard touchdown in the win. The unit remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cam Skattebo totals 100 yards Sunday
items.desc: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught 3-of-4 targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: On Sunday, Skattebo was practically New York's entire offense. He was the team's leader in rushing and receiving yards, and he nearly doubled the yards of the next closest skill-position player. His workload is elite at this point, but he isn't likely to be a strong fantasy option moving forward given how weak this New York offense is looking without QB Jaxson Dart (knee).

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jameis Winston doesn't score in win Sunday
items.desc: Jameis Winston completed 14-of-22 passing attempts for 118 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Winston got the start for the Giants on Sunday, but it didn't look the best. He wasn't able to lead New York's offense to a single touchdown against one of the NFL's worst defenses in the Titans, but they were still able to come away with the win. It looks like Winston, and nearly all of New York's offense, is going to be irrelevant moving forward.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Rachaad White catches touchdown in Week 3 win over Seahawks
items.desc: Rachaad White rushed eight times for 35 yards while also hauling in his only target for six yards and one touchdown in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: White has heated up out of the backfield of late, finishing with 40 or more offensive yards in each of the first two contests. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as part of a backfield shared with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Terry McLaurin leads pass-catchers in Week 3 win over Seahawks
items.desc: Terry McLaurin hauled in six of his nine targets for 77 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: McLaurin has heated up in the Washington offense of late, registering 50 or more receiving yards in each of the last two contests. The wideout offers fantasy managers one of the few explosive options in the Washington passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Stefon Diggs hauls in four passes in Week 3 win
items.desc: Stefon Diggs hauled in four of his seven targets  for 33 yards in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: Diggs has made the most of his involvement in the Washington passing attack early on, recording four or more receptions in each of the first three games. The veteran wideout remains one of the few stable pass-catching options in an inconsistent offense to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt bottled up in Week 3 win
items.desc: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 19 times for 36 yards while also hauling in his only target for seven yards in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: Croskey-Merritt has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield of late, rushing for less than 50 yards in each of the last two games. The running back remains a risky lineup option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Antonio Williams quiet in Week 3 win
items.desc: Antonio Williams caught two of his four targets for 15 yards in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: Williams has fallen back to earth after an impressive showing in Week 1, finishing with less than 25 receiving yards in each of the last two games. The wideout remains a risky-pass catching option in an inconsistent offense early on, with a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Dyami Brown sees one target in Week 3
items.desc: Dyami Brown failed to catch his only target in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: Brown has seen minimal involvement in the Washington offense early on, posting two targets or less in two of the first three games. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: De'Von Achane (knee) suffers season-ending torn ACL
items.desc: De'Von Achane (knee) suffered a season ending torn ACL against the Chiefs.
items.impact: Achane went down early in the Dolphins contest against Kansas City, with Ollie Gordon filling in as the primary rusher in his absence. Gordon is now a primary pickup for fantasy, and Jaylen Wright is worth a pickup as well.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ben Sinnott sees one target in Week 3
items.desc: Ben Sinnott failed to catch his only target in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: Sinnott has been non existent in the Washington offense to begin the season, recording one target or less in each of the first three games. The tight end remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: John Bates catches pass in Week 3
items.desc: John Bates caught his lone target for nine yards in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: Bates has underwhelmed to begin the season, recording two catches or less in each of his three contests. The tight end remains another risky pass-catching option in the Washington offense early on, with a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Treylon Burks catches touchdown in Week 3 win
items.desc: Treylon Burks caught both of his targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: Burks has made minimal impact in the Washington passing attack early on, finishing with less than 15 receiving yards in each of his two games. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Colson Yankoff quiet in Week 3
items.desc: Colson Yankoff caught one of his two targets for two yards in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: Yankoff has been an afterthought in the Washington passing attack early on, recording two targets or less in each of his two contests. The tight end can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jaylin Lane catches pass in Week 3
items.desc: Jaylin Lane caught his only target for 21 yards in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
items.impact: Lane has struggled to make an impact to begin the season, finishing with one reception or less in each of the first three games. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Drew Stevens misses extra point in Week 3
items.desc: Drew Stevens converted both of his field goal attempts as well as 3-of-4 extra point attempts to finish with nine points in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: Stevens has battled consistency issues early on, missing an extra point attempt in two of the first three contests. The kicker will look to right the ship beginning in Week 4 against the Indianapolis Colts.
